extracted.intended_audience: engineers and general readers interested in early locomotive design and railway history
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria, practices, and trial conditions for designing, constructing, and evaluating early steam locomotives and associated railway infrastructure, as described in a historical engineering account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of locomotive power for public railways
rubrics_metrics.description: Greater convenience of locomotive power for the purposes of a public highway; likened to a series of short unconnected chains, any one of which could be removed and another substituted without interruption to the traffic; contrasted with fixed engine system as a continuous chain whose failure of any link would derange the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a power system allows modular replacement and continuity of traffic; consider convenience for public use and resilience to single-point failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiler heating-surface and evaporative capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrangement of the boiler and the extension of its heating surface to enable steam enough to be raised rapidly and continuously; the effect of high-pressure engines depends mainly upon the quantity of steam which the boiler can generate and its degree of elasticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design boilers with sufficient heating surface relative to fuel consumption and furnace temperature to sustain required high-pressure steam and continuous operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of steam-blast (exhaust into chimney) to increase draught
rubrics_metrics.description: Stimulating combustion in the furnace by throwing the waste steam into the chimney after performing its office in the cylinders, thus accelerating the ascent of the current of air, greatly increasing the draught, and consequently the temperature of the fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt exhaust-blast arrangements to intensify draught and combustion; measure effects on fire intensity and overall economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-off: increased heating surface vs engine weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Lengthening boilers and increasing surface by flue-tubes raises evaporative power but also increased engine weight (example: double-tube engine weighed ~12 tons, exceeding 6-ton competition limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance gains in steam production from larger heating surfaces against weight constraints and operational limits; optimize for permitted weight and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multitubular/tubular boiler principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Employing multiple tubes (horizontal or small perpendicular tubes) through which heated air passes, surrounded by the water of the boiler, to materially increase heating surface (e.g., Rocket: 25 copper tubes, 3 in diameter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tubular boilers to extend heating surface and evaporative efficiency; monitor for fouling, tube failure, and maintenance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of tube fouling and burn-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Early attempts with tubes containing water became furred with deposit, shortly burned out and were removed; poor arrangements can lead to early failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tube layouts and water circulation to minimise fouling; specify maintenance/cleaning regimes and materials to resist deposit and overheating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing/joining method for boiler tubes to prevent leakage
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit smooth copper tubes tightly into bored boiler ends, solder up, and then raise the steam so that the expansion of the tubes fills interstices and produces a perfectly watertight boiler capable of withstanding extreme internal pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise fitting and soldering, and rely on thermal expansion to seal tube joints; validate with hydraulic pressure testing and iterative fitting if initial leaks occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimization of blast-pipe orifice (contraction) for draught vs piston vacuum
rubrics_metrics.description: Contraction of the blast-pipe increases draught but may produce negative pressure upon the piston; experiments with different pipe diameters measured rarefaction to determine optimal contraction (Rocket: blast-pipes contracted slightly below area of steam-ports; water rose 3 inches in test tube).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimentally determine blast-pipe geometry to maximize draught without unacceptable piston vacuum; quantify rarefaction and measure combustion and performance trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fire-box design and being surrounded by water
rubrics_metrics.description: Fire-box (furnace) attached immediately behind the boiler and also surrounded with water (example dimensions: 2 ft wide and 3 ft high), contributing to heating surface and steam generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the fire-box is sized and water-jacketed to support continuous high steam output; coordinate dimensions with tube arrangement and boiler capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cylinder placement and direct drive arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Cylinders placed on each side of the boiler in an oblique position with direct connection from piston-rod to a pin on the outside of the driving wheel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cylinder positioning and direct drive to wheels for mechanical simplicity and efficient power transmission; evaluate kinematics and alignment to avoid undue wear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition/trial weight and dimensional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Engines admitted to competitions were subject to strict weight limits (example: six tons for Liverpool competition); exceeding stipulated weight could disqualify or influence judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design within explicit competition or operational weight limits; account for tender, water, and fuel when calculating admitted weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed trial performance conditions (distance, trips, average speed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each engine was required to make twenty trips, equal to 70 miles in the day, and the average rate of travelling was to be not under 10 miles an hour; engines tried separately and on different days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate engines under the exact trial conditions specified; plan for endurance (many repeated trips), average speed targets, and isolated testing to avoid confounding variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliable steam-raising time and safety-valve operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Raising steam until safety-valve loaded to a specified pressure (example: 50 lb/sq in), and the time required to get up steam (example: 57 minutes) were part of pre-trial preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify acceptable steam-raising time and safety-valve pressure thresholds for readiness; ensure boiler can reach and hold required pressure safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fuel economy and consumption as evaluation metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive fuel consumption (example: Novelty wasted about 692 lbs coke per hour when travelling) was a practical objection and factor against a design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure fuel consumption at operating speeds and loads; designs with high fuel loss (e.g., blowing fuel out via blast) are penalised for inefficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability and durability under repeated trips
rubrics_metrics.description: Engines must perform all stipulated trips without breakdowns (breakdowns in pumps, boilers, bellows etc. led to failure in trials); repeated failures could lead judges to refuse further trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise robustness of pumps, boiler integrity, feed systems, and moving parts to ensure continuous operation across many trips; include spare parts and pre-trial checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability to exceed stipulated performance sustainably
rubrics_metrics.description: Rocket performed beyond stipulated conditions (average 15 mph vs required 10 mph; reached 29–35 mph) demonstrating headroom and sustainable over-performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design with margin beyond requirements to allow sustained higher speeds and loads without approaching failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Way maintenance and track integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Every rail with its fastenings must be complete to prevent risk of accident; road must be kept regularly ballasted up to the level to diminish jolting of vehicles at high speeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish maintenance regimes for rails, fastenings, and ballast to ensure track geometry, reduce vibrations, and prevent accidents at high speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal visibility and stopping distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Stations must be protected by signals observable from such a distance as to enable the train to be stopped in event of an obstacle; early practice used men with flags before fixed signals or telegraphing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide signalling systems with sufficient sighting/lead distance (or telegraphic communication) to allow safe stopping; test visibility in operating conditions and at required speeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rail strength appropriate to traffic and locomotive weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Original iron roads (fish-bellied rails 35 lb/yd) proved too weak for heavier locomotives; heavier and stronger rails became necessary at increased expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify rail section and fastening strength matched to expected axle loads and traffic intensity; plan for incremental upgrades as locomotive weights rise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of passenger rolling stock for safety and comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: Passenger-carriage novel structure: mounted on strong framing, supported on springs to prevent jolting; measures to prevent hard bumping (buffer-springs) and to improve brakes and axle lubrication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design carriages with spring-suspended frames, effective buffers, reliable brakes, and proper lubrication to ensure passenger comfort and reduce wear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coupling devices and train handling (coupling screw invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention of the coupling screw (Henry Booth) for rolling stock arrangements used in passenger railways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate coupling systems that control carriage spacing and allow safe, mechanical transmission of buffers and braking forces across the train.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brake systems and self-acting brake concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-acting brake: fit each carriage with a brake called into action immediately when the locomotive is pulled up; the momentum drives buffer-springs and simultaneously actuates brakes to bring wheels into a state of 'sledge' and stop the train; later revived with centrifugal apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider distributed braking systems that automatically engage upon locomotive braking, using mechanical linkages or centrifugal aids; validate effectiveness and risk of simultaneous wheel locking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliable water-feed and pump systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Failures of cold-water pumps prevented engines (e.g., Sanspareil) from continuing trials; adequate water supply and pump reliability are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and test feedwater systems and pumps for reliability under trial/fleet conditions; include redundancy or preventive maintenance where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial administration: separate trials and fairness of judging
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid confusion each engine should be tried separately and on different days; judges may refuse additional trials if prior performance indicates unreliability or contravention of published conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administer trials with controlled, repeatable conditions per entrant; judges should enforce stated rules (weight limits, design acceptability) and avoid ad hoc allowances that compromise fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of novel design acceptability beyond raw performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges refused to recommend an engine constructed on a plan they 'could not recommend for adoption by the directors' even if it attempted to run despite being over weight; design acceptability and future operability mattered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess designs not just on single-run metrics but on maintainability, safety, fuel economy, and suitability for adoption in regular service; questionable design principles can outweigh isolated performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of blast geometry on fuel loss (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive sharpness of steam-blast may blow burning fuel into the air, causing enormous fuel waste (example: Novelty's sharp blast caused waste of coke).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blast configurations that cause entrainment of burning fuel; evaluate combustion efficiency and particulate/fuel loss as part of blast design.
